intro.title: Every handoff is part of the journey.
paragraphs: Ethio Rail Logistics brings the practical stages of cargo movement into one connected service view, from inland transport and rail to customs, warehousing, ports, and international freight.

metadata.description: Learn how Ethio Rail Logistics combines railway capability and private-sector logistics experience to coordinate multimodal cargo movement.

hero.title: Built around connected movement.
hero.description: Ethio Rail Logistics is an Ethiopian multimodal logistics company established through Ethiopian Railways Corporation and GetAs International PLC.
hero.imageAlt: Ethiopian Railway locomotive on the rail corridor.

intro.title: Rail capability meets logistics experience.
paragraphs: Ethio Rail Logistics combines railway capability with private-sector logistics experience across road and rail coordination, sea transport, customs, freight forwarding, warehousing, terminals, cargo handling, and integrated logistics management.
The purpose is to reduce fragmentation in cargo movement and provide more coordinated end-to-end logistics services around the needs of each shipment.

metadata.description: Explore the working direction behind EthioRail’s connected logistics and corridor-focused approach.

hero.title: A direction for connected logistics.
hero.description: This page describes the working direction of EthioRail’s logistics approach without presenting unverified prose as an official corporate statement.
hero.imageAlt: Rail freight containers being handled along the Ethiopian railway.

intro.title: A direction for connected and sustainable logistics.
paragraphs: Our mission is to provide efficient and cost-effective multimodal transport solutions by integrating the strengths of different transport modes to improve delivery times, reduce logistics costs, and minimize environmental impact.
Our vision is to become a leading provider of integrated logistics solutions that connect Ethiopia to global trade while advancing efficient and sustainable transportation.

ERL supports and coordinates the customs process with the customer and responsible authorities; approval remains with the responsible authority.

journey.title: Connect each stage of the journey.

steps.title: Pre-clearance / Pre-arrival review
steps.description: Review shipment information and available documentation before cargo arrival where applicable.

steps.title: Document preparation
steps.description: Coordinate commercial invoices, packing lists, transport documents, permits, certificates and other required shipment information.

steps.title: Customs declaration
steps.description: Support preparation and coordination of information needed for the applicable customs declaration process.

steps.title: Assessment & regulatory coordination
steps.description: Coordinate required classification, valuation information and applicable regulatory requirements.

steps.title: Inspection / verification
steps.description: Support documentation, scanning or physical inspection coordination when requested by responsible authorities.

steps.title: Duties, taxes & requirements
steps.description: Support the customer in coordinating applicable payment and document requirements.

steps.title: Customs release
steps.description: After approval by the responsible authority, connect the cargo with the next logistics stage.

steps.title: Onward movement
steps.description: Connect customs release with terminal, rail, inland transport, warehousing or final delivery.

metadata.title: Multimodal Transportation | Ethio Rail Logistics
metadata.description: Connected road, rail, inland, port, and ocean logistics stages for coordinated cargo movement.

hero.title: One journey. Multiple modes. One coordinated movement.
hero.description: EthioRail coordinates movement across road, rail, inland logistics points, ports, and ocean connections as part of a connected cargo journey.
hero.imageAlt: Ethiopian Railway freight train and container handling equipment at an intermodal terminal.

overview.title: Different modes, understood as one journey.
paragraphs: Multimodal transportation brings more than one transport mode into a coordinated cargo movement. Road connections, rail corridors, inland logistics points, port gateways, and ocean routes can each have a place in the same journey.
The service is about making those transitions easier to understand and coordinate, so the movement is planned around the route and the cargo rather than treated as a series of disconnected handoffs.

journey.title: A connected sequence from origin to destination.

steps.title: Origin / Cargo Collection
steps.description: Cargo begins at its origin and is prepared for the first connection.

steps.title: Road Connection
steps.description: Inland road movement connects the origin with the next logistics point.

steps.title: Inland Logistics / Dry Port
steps.description: Cargo can be staged, handled, or transferred as the journey changes mode.

steps.title: Rail Corridor
steps.description: Rail provides a corridor connection for the next part of the movement.

steps.title: Port Connection
steps.description: The inland journey connects toward a port and its gateway operations.

steps.title: Ocean / International Connection
steps.description: Cargo can continue through ocean and international trade connections.

steps.title: Destination
steps.description: The journey concludes with the final connection to its destination.

modes.title: Each mode has a role in the movement.

items.description: Corridor movement linking inland cargo flows with regional gateways.

items.description: Cargo handling, staging, and dry-port connections between modes.

items.title: Port
items.description: Gateway connection where inland movement meets maritime logistics.

items.title: Ocean
items.description: International onward movement toward wider trade routes and destinations.

corridor.title: Built around the Ethiopia–Djibouti corridor.
corridor.description: The Ethiopia–Djibouti corridor connects inland Ethiopian cargo flows toward Djibouti and international maritime gateways. The route gives multimodal planning a clear geographic context without reducing every shipment to the same sequence.
corridor.imageAlt: Ethiopia–Djibouti corridor map showing Addis Ababa, Dire Dawa, Djibouti, and global markets.

overview.title: Terminal coordination around the wider cargo journey.
paragraphs: ERL coordinates dry-port and terminal activities as part of the wider cargo journey, including services connected through Modjo and Dire Dawa.

metadata.description: From order planning to final delivery, connect supply chain requirements in one coordinated plan.

hero.title: From order planning to final delivery.
hero.description: ERL works with customers to structure logistics around the complete supply chain rather than only one transport leg. The solution can connect order coordination, shipment readiness, pre-clearance, consolidation, transportation, warehousing, value-added services and final delivery around one coordinated plan.

overview.title: From order planning to final delivery.
paragraphs: ERL works with customers to structure logistics around the complete supply chain rather than only one transport leg.

The solution can connect order coordination, shipment readiness, pre-clearance, consolidation, transportation, warehousing, value-added services and final delivery around one coordinated plan. Scope and availability are confirmed through shipment review and the logistics network.
